The claim states that the work on adaptive surface extraction from anisotropic volumetric data describes a topological refinement aspect (Local Refinement and Manifold Verification) to address non-manifold configurations arising from local subdivision. Source [S2] explicitly describes an algorithm to solve non-manifold configurations caused by local subdivision. It details a process of extracting information about the shape of the boundary in face-adjacent cells, building a quadtree, applying complex face/edge tests, and recursively refining (subdividing) cells if complexity is detected. The source also explicitly mentions that this approach is guided by topological complexity and differs from previous methods by not limiting fixes to neighboring cells with a small level difference. The caption for Figure 6 in [S2] also refers to the 'local refinement and manifold verification algorithm'. Therefore, all facts in the claim are present and supported by the evidence.
